expectations.text: States the 14-day rule with its criteria: apply updates within 14 days when vendor-rated critical or high risk, OR CVSS v3 base score 7.0+, OR no vendor severity detail provided
expectations.evidence: 'within 14 days... vendor describes the fix as "critical" or "high risk"... OR CVSS v3 base score of 7.0 or above, OR the vendor gives no severity detail at all'

expectations.text: Covers automatic updates: enable them wherever possible
expectations.evidence: 'Enabling automatic updates wherever the platform supports it is the practical way'

expectations.text: Handles unsupported software correctly: Windows Server 2012 (out of support) must be REMOVED, or moved out of scope into a defined sub-set that blocks ALL internet traffic both directions — keeping it in scope is a certification failure
expectations.evidence: 'must either be removed entirely... or moved out of scope into a clearly segregated sub-set... ALL internet traffic - inbound and outbound - is blocked'; 'unsupported software sitting inside your certified scope is an automatic certification failure'

expectations.text: Notes the 14-day update questions are automatic-fail questions under the current (Danzell) marking
expectations.evidence: 'A6.4... and A6.5 (applications) - are automatic-fail questions' under Danzell

expectations.text: Mentions firmware counts as software (with firewall/router firmware needing make/model listing)
expectations.evidence: 'Firmware counts as software here too, so your router/firewall firmware... you'll need to be able to list its make and model'
